claims.text: An optimal sub-stoichiometric Al level promotes controlled lattice distortion in Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni alloys.
The Al-induced lattice distortion stabilizes a disordered single-phase FCC or BCC structure by balancing atomic-size-mismatch strain and mixing enthalpy.
The optimized disordered state enables concurrent retention of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
The equiatomic or near-equiatomic Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni baseline has mixed phase content that may include a disordered solid solution and precipitated intermetallic phases.
Reducing Al below its equiatomic level can avoid ordering.
Higher Al contents tend to produce ordered or intermetallic phases.
Atomic-size mismatch between Al and the other constituent elements induces lattice distortion.
Al-induced lattice distortion influences local chemical order and short-range-order parameters.
At an optimal Al level, lattice strain disrupts long-range ordering tendencies.
Disruption of long-range ordering suppresses the formation of deleterious intermetallic phases.
Suppressing intermetallic formation produces a homogeneous disordered solid solution with a high density of obstacles to dislocation motion.
The high density of obstacles to dislocation motion enhances high-temperature strength.
The high density of obstacles to dislocation motion enhances radiation-damage resistance.
A homogeneous disordered solid solution minimizes corrosion pathways.
A homogeneous disordered solid solution maintains ductility at cryogenic temperatures.
Relative to the equiatomic baseline, an optimally reduced Al alloy will exhibit a single-phase disordered structure.

Relative to the equiatomic baseline, an optimally reduced Al alloy will have enhanced high-temperature yield strength, improved corrosion resistance, improved radiation resistance, and retained or improved cryogenic toughness.
Excessively high Al content will produce ordered phases or intermetallic precipitates that degrade at least one target property.
The proposed composition-property relationship is limited to Al variation within the Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni system under controlled processing conditions.
No direct evidence is provided that quantitatively correlates Al-induced lattice distortion with suppression of intermetallic formation across the full service-temperature and irradiation range.
